classification.difficultyReason: Model the limiting ray through the awning's outer edge and the window's bottom, interpret why this gives the least angle, and apply inverse tangent with the angle measured from the vertical window.

content.prompt: A horizontal awning that has a depth of 80 cm is attached to the top of a window of height 2 m. What is the least angle that a ray of sunlight can make with the window if no light is to shine directly into it? Give your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a degree.

answer.short:
$21.8^\circ$.

Use the limiting ray from the outer edge of the awning to the bottom of the window, measuring the angle from the vertical.
answer.worked:
The limiting ray passes through the outer edge of the awning and the bottom of the window. Let $\theta$ be its angle with the vertical window. The right triangle has horizontal side $80\text{ cm}=0.8\text{ m}$ and vertical side 2 m.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{0.8}{2}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}(0.4)\\\theta&\approx21.8^\circ\end{align*}$$

At a smaller angle to the window, sunlight reaches part of the window below the awning's shadow.
